summary: Jean Petitot is a philosopher and linguist who studied at École Polytechnique from circa 1963 to 1966. He later served as director at École Polytechnique from circa 1999 to 2006.

Jean Philippe Vogel was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who studied at the University of Amsterdam under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1901–1914) and as director at Leiden University (1914–1939).

Jean Przyluski was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who studied under Henri Hubert and Marcel Mauss. He served as professor at INALCO (1913–1930), EPHE (1926–1944), and Collège de France (1930–1944).

Jean-Baptiste Biot was a physicist and Indologist who studied at École Polytechnique under Gaspard Monge and Pierre-Simon Laplace. His main academic posts included professor of physics at the Collège de France (1800–1862) and at the Science Faculty of Paris (1809–1862).

Jean-François Jarrige was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Paris and studied at École du Louvre. He served as director and head of the Musée Guimet from 1986 to 2008.

Jean-François Lyotard was a philosopher who studied at the University of Paris and Paris Nanterre University. He held positions at Paris 8 University Vincennes-Saint-Denis (1972–1987), UC Irvine (circa 1987–1993), and Emory University (circa 1993–1998).
Jean-François Revel was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Jean-Baptiste-Say, Lycée du Parc (~1941–1943), and the École Normale Supérieure in 1943.

Jean-Louis Burnouf was a classicist who studied at Collège d'Harcourt and under Alexander Hamilton and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy. He was professor of rhetoric at Collège Louis-le-Grand (~1808–1826) and held the Latin eloquence chair at Collège de France (1816–1844).
Jean-Luc Achard is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a post at the CNRS, attested in 2003–2004.
Jean-Luc Chevillard is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure in 1975 under Antoine Culioli. He served as a researcher at the CNRS from circa 1989 to 2021.

Jean-Noël Robert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology who studied at INALCO and under Bernard Frank. He held posts at the CNRS (1975–1990), EPHE (from 1979), and Collège de France (2010–2022).

Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat was a Sinologist and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He held the chair of Sinology at the Collège de France (1814–1832) and served as conservator and president at the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Jean-Pierre Drège is a Sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at INALCO and the University of Burgundy Europe under Yves Hervouet. He served as president of the École Française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1998 to 2004.

Jeannine Auboyer was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at École du Louvre, the Sorbonne, and EPHE under mentors including René Grousset and Jean Przyluski. She served as chief curator at Musée Guimet and held a chair at École du Louvre (1965–1980).

Jeff Dolven is a scholar of English who studied at the University of Oxford and Yale University. He was a junior fellow at the Harvard Society of Fellows (~1996–1999) and became a professor of English at Princeton University circa 1999.

Jeff Malpas is a philosopher who studied at the University of Auckland and the Australian National University. He headed the philosophy programme at Murdoch University (~1989–1999) and was appointed professor at the University of Tasmania in 1999.
Jeff Watt is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied under Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima. He held a post at the Rubin Museum of Art.
Jeff Wilson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He studied under mentors Taitetsu Unno and Akio Tatsuguchi.

Jeffery D. Long is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his BA at the University of Notre Dame and his PhD at the University of Chicago Divinity School, becoming associate professor at Elizabethtown College in 2000.

Jeffrey L. Broughton is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1975. He was a professor in the Department of Religious Studies at California State University, Long Beach (attested 2004).
